result.title: Reasoning in the loop: antibody lead optimization by probing mechanism and measurement
result.summary: Lab-in-the-loop systems, in which a model proposes molecules, automated assays measure their properties and the results retrain the model, are a popular approach to antibody lead optimization. These systems optimize for a specification defined with metrics computed from instrument signals, so their success depends on how well those metrics serve as proxies for the properties a drug candidate needs. When a metric is a poor proxy, neither a better model nor more data will fix it, and identifying the problem usually requires expert review. We report two campaigns run on BigHat Biosciences' Milliner platform, one on an anti-albumin nanobody (VHH) and one on an anti-mesothelin single-chain variable fragment (scFv), in which a research team and a general-purpose AI agent, Claude, brought scientific reasoning into the loop. Over seven rounds and about 1,010 design variants we built libraries from antibody lineage, structure and biophysics, and found from the raw curves that on each scaffold one thermal metric did not measure what its name implied. The libraries were built as controlled comparisons, so the results also show what each mutation contributes to each property. We fit a physical model of the curves, used it to choose metrics suited to each scaffold, and changed the experimental protocol, varying protein concentration and heating rate, to test the model against pre-registered predictions. Both leads improve on their parents in affinity, thermal stability and aggregation while improving or maintaining yield and purity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文报告两个基于 Milliner 平台的抗体先导优化闭环实验：研究团队与通用 AI agent（Claude）共同将科学推理引入 lab-in-the-loop，在七轮、约 1010 个设计变体中构建受控对比文库，从原始测量曲线发现每个 scaffold 上均有一个热稳定性指标并不度量其名称所指的性质，进而拟合物理模型、改用适配 scaffold 的指标并调整实验协议做预注册验证，获得在亲和力、热稳定性与聚集上优于亲本且产量纯度不降的先导。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「闭环探测某一指标是否真在度量其名义属性、并用预注册预测检验模型」的思路，可能启发 LVR 中 latent 相似度与探针指标效度的核查、证据筛选及停止决策设计，但领域距离较远，可迁移性需核查。
